messages:
Alyssa S.: hey team — Acme wants a short POC using a Dedicated endpoint but they require static egress IPs for their firewall allowlist. they also want webhooks from model function-calls to hit their on-prem service. POC target date next tuesday. what are our tradeoffs + fastest path?

Raj P.: two quick options: 1) managed dedicated pool with static egress (we assign a small set of public IPs/NAT) — fastest to spin up for a POC (2–5 business days prep) and minimal customer infra. 2) private deployment into customer VPC (VPC peering or customer-hosted) — fully isolated, single-tenant networking, but multi-week and needs infra access. for an asap POC go with option 1. :thumbsup:

Marta L.: technical notes for option 1: we provide an egress IP block (typically a /29) and all outbound traffic from the dedicated pool will SNAT to those IPs. webhooks and function-calls will originate from those IPs on port 443. customer must allow outbound DNS (to resolve our hostnames) and allow inbound traffic for their callback endpoint from our IPs. sample allowlist block for them:```13.32.45.200/29:443```

Marta L.: also note TLS only on 443; we do not support arbitrary ports. we do not support mutual TLS for outbound callbacks right now — only server TLS. if they need mTLS, recommend Private deployment or a reverse proxy in their network.

Kai T.: add security checklist items: confirm SOC2 status, encrypt-at-rest/HSM for keys, logging retention, and whether they need traffic to remain in-region. if they insist on immutable single-IP guarantees during bursts, option 1 might not suffice — bursts could use adjacent IPs in the same block. make sure customer signs off on that.

Raj P.: pricing heads-up: dedicated egress + pool setup has a one-time provisioning fee and reserved monthly commit for GPUs. for a POC we can offer a short-term reduced commit / credits — I’ll draft numbers.

Alyssa S.: customer asked for exact text they can paste into their firewall team. Marta, can you give a copy-paste snippet?

Marta L.: sure — they can paste:```# Allow Redwood POC outbound
13.32.45.200/29 tcp 443 # Redwood managed egress (POC)
# DNS: allow outbound UDP/TCP 53 to their existing resolvers
```

Raj P.: also include DNS hostnames: `pocec2.reddw-inference.net` (example) — they should allow SNI/hostname validation on their firewall if possible.

Alyssa S.: customer also worried about webhook retries and source IPs if we failover. do we preserve IPs across failover?

Marta L.: failover within the same dedicated region should keep egress within the assigned block, but cross-region failover could use different blocks. we can add a note in the SOW: failover may change source IPs if we route to another region.

Kai T.: for the security questionnaire question about data residency and egress logs: we can provide logs showing outbound IPs and TLS handshakes for the POC timeframe. include that in answers.

Raj P.: action items: (1) I will draft a POC quote and include temporary credits + expected lead time (2–5 business days for managed egress). (2) Marta to provide exact CIDR and SOW language. (3) Kai to prepare security QA responses. I’ll open a provisioning ticket.

InfraBot: provisioning ticket created: INF-4721 — dedicated-pool-egress-provision (owner: Raj P.). ETA initial IP block assignment: 72 hours. :robot_face:

Alyssa S.: perfect — I’ll send this to Acme and ask them to confirm their firewall contact and callback endpoint FQDN. will update thread with the customer's security questionnaire items when they arrive. thanks all! :pray:
